title: Longest Non-decreasing Subarray From Two Arrays
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, create a new array nums3 by choosing elements from either nums1 or nums2 at each index to maximize the length of the longest non-decreasing subarray in nums3.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, create a new array nums3 by choosing elements from either nums1 or nums2 at each index to maximize the length of the longest non-decreasing subarray in nums3. Return the length of this subarray.
constraints: At each index choose either nums1[i] or nums2[i].
Find the longest contiguous index interval whose chosen values are nondecreasing.
hints: Track two suffix lengths, ending with the choice from nums1 or nums2 at the current index.
Each new ending can extend either previous ending when its value is at least the chosen predecessor.
Compute four comparisons using saved prior states and keep the global maximum.
The ending choice and preceding ending choice are the only information needed to characterize every nondecreasing suffix.
editorial: The ending choice and preceding ending choice are the only information needed to characterize every nondecreasing suffix.

tests.explanation: Choosing 1,2 over the first two indices gives a nondecreasing interval of length two.
Choosing 1,2,2,4 across all indices gives length four.
